hardware.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

timing_units: seconds; the accompanying document rounds to whole seconds as XmYs
scope: Actual saved Init proof; warm proving uses prepared SRS, reused fixed preprocessing and prepared PLONK keys. Initial aggregation, FRI compression, builds and parameter provisioning are excluded from proving times. One-time PLONK key preparation is recorded separately. Default CPU parallelism and uncontrolled OS page caches.

bn254_gpu.scope: Externally pinned existing Init artifacts; same loaded circuit, keys and witness for CPU and CUDA, fresh gnark blinding. No compilation or key preparation.
bn254_gpu.measurement_limitations: Three paired rounds in one process with loaded keys, fresh CUDA context per proof, no forced GC, default CPU parallelism. Core timers exclude initial artifact loading and per-proof backend setup. Host RSS is shared-process peak, not isolated per-backend peak; device samples are two-second lower bounds.
bn254_gpu.standalone_gpu_memory_note: Two-second device polling missed the short allocation peak in this standalone run; native pool high-water marks are authoritative for allocations managed by that pool, excluding driver and other allocations. The comparison retains the repeated benchmark device-memory sample.
bn254_gpu.standalone_scope: One production CLI proof in a fresh process with prepared keys, artifact authentication/loading, witness assembly, CUDA setup, proving, verification and serialization; default CPU parallelism; one GPU; OS page cache uncontrolled.
